sourceRecords.title: California Revenue and Taxation Code section 17041, Personal Income Tax, Imposition of Tax
sourceRecords.retrievalNote: Retrieved in the implementation session. Subdivision (a)(1) imposes the tax for each taxable year upon THE ENTIRE TAXABLE INCOME of every resident who is not a part-year resident, at the rates in a single table, and subdivision (c)(1) does the same for a head of household. Neither subdivision states a separate schedule, band or rate for any class of income, which is what this pack cites for its declaration that it carries no preferential treatment. Subdivision (h) requires the Franchise Tax Board to RECOMPUTE the income tax brackets prescribed in subdivisions (a) and (c) for each taxable year beginning on or after January 1, 1988, by multiplying the preceding taxable year brackets by an inflation adjustment factor. The bracket dollar amounts printed in the statute are therefore a pre-indexing base and are NOT the schedule for any recent taxable year; this pack carries none of them and derives none of them. publishedAt records the January 1, 2011 effective date the retrieved document states for its last amendment.

sourceRecords.title: California Revenue and Taxation Code section 17043, additional tax on taxable income in excess of one million dollars
sourceRecords.retrievalNote: Retrieved in the implementation session. Subdivision (a) reads: For each taxable year beginning on or after January 1, 2005, in addition to any other taxes imposed by this part, an additional tax shall be imposed at the rate of 1 percent on that portion of a taxpayer's taxable income in excess of one million dollars ($1,000,000). That sentence states the rate, the threshold and the years the section applies to, and the stated range beginning January 1 2005 and carrying no end contains the declared tax year, which is what this pack's indexing.declaredFor records. Subdivision (c) states that three provisions shall NOT apply to the tax imposed by this section: (1) Section 17039, relating to the allowance of credits; (2) Section 17041, relating to filing status and recomputation of the income tax brackets; and (3) Section 17045, relating to joint returns. Item (1) is why no credit reaches this leg. Items (2) and (3) are why the threshold is identical for every filing status, including a joint return, and why it is not recomputed for inflation. The section was added by initiative Proposition 63, section 12, operative January 1, 2005, which is the date publishedAt records.

sourceRecords.title: California Revenue and Taxation Code section 17039, allowance of credits and the definition of net tax
sourceRecords.retrievalNote: Retrieved in the implementation session. Subdivision (a) reads in relevant part: for the purposes of computing tax credits, the term net tax means the tax imposed under either Section 17041 or 17048 plus the tax imposed under Section 17504 LESS THE CREDITS ALLOWED BY SECTION 17054 (relating to personal exemption credits), and then states that credits shall be allowed against net tax in a numbered order. A credit that is subtracted from a tax already imposed under Section 17041 is applied AFTER rate application and is not a reduction of income; that sentence is what this pack cites for its relief mechanism's kind and application point. The section states the ORDER of credits; it states no exemption credit AMOUNT, and none is transcribed from it. publishedAt records the September 19, 2025 effective date the retrieved document states for its last amendment.

sourceRecords.title: California Revenue and Taxation Code section 17073.5, election to take a standard deduction and its annual recomputation
sourceRecords.retrievalNote: Retrieved in this session to test whether the standard deduction could be sourced from statute rather than from a Franchise Tax Board publication. It cannot. Subdivision (a) states two dollar amounts, and subdivision (d) then reads: For each taxable year beginning on or after January 1, 1988, the Franchise Tax Board shall RECOMPUTE the standard deduction amounts prescribed in subdivision (a), multiplying the preceding taxable year's amounts by an inflation adjustment factor built from a California Consumer Price Index change that paragraph (1) requires the California Department of Industrial Relations to transmit no later than AUGUST 1 OF THE CURRENT CALENDAR YEAR. The amounts printed in subdivision (a) are therefore a pre-indexing base and are NOT the deduction for any recent taxable year; this pack carries neither of them and derives nothing from them. Two structural facts ARE taken from this section and are the only things it supplies here: subdivision (a) places a head of household and a surviving spouse with a joint return rather than with a single filer, and subdivision (d)(4) states that the joint-class amount shall be twice the single-class amount. publishedAt records the August 20, 1998 effective date the retrieved document states for its last amendment.

sourceRecords.title: California Revenue and Taxation Code section 17054, credits for personal exemption and their annual computation
sourceRecords.retrievalNote: Retrieved in this session to test whether the exemption credit amounts could be sourced from statute rather than from a Franchise Tax Board publication. They cannot. Subdivisions (a) and (b) state dollar amounts, and subdivision (i) then reads: For each taxable year beginning on or after January 1, 1989, the Franchise Tax Board shall COMPUTE the credits prescribed in this section, multiplying the immediately preceding taxable year's credits by an inflation adjustment factor built from a California Consumer Price Index change that paragraph (1) requires the California Department of Industrial Relations to transmit no later than AUGUST 1 OF THE CURRENT CALENDAR YEAR. The amounts printed in subdivisions (a) and (b) are therefore a pre-indexing base and are NOT the credit for any recent taxable year; this pack carries none of them and derives nothing from them. The opening sentence corroborates the application point this pack already cites from section 17039: the credits MAY BE DEDUCTED FROM THE TAX IMPOSED UNDER SECTION 17041, which is a subtraction from tax and not from income. Subdivision (i)(4) states that the joint-return credit shall be twice the single credit. publishedAt records the January 1, 2021 effective date the retrieved document states for its last amendment.

supportedFeatures.label: Established order of deduction, rate application, surcharge and credit
supportedFeatures.reason: Section 17041(a) imposes the tax on the entire taxable income at its schedule, section 17043(a) imposes the additional one-percent tax on taxable income in excess of one million dollars in addition to any other tax imposed by the part, and section 17039(a) defines net tax as the tax imposed under section 17041 less the personal exemption credits. Those three retrieved sentences establish the order this pack declares, so the pack ships rather than refusing in full.

supportedFeatures.label: No preferential schedule for qualified dividends or long-term capital gain
supportedFeatures.reason: Section 17041(a)(1) and (c)(1) impose the tax upon the entire taxable income at one schedule and state no separate schedule, band or rate for any class of income. The pack therefore declares preferentialPolicy none and carries no preferential table, and the engine prices pooled preferential income in the ordinary schedule with no branch of its own.

supportedFeatures.label: Additional one-percent tax above one million dollars of taxable income
supportedFeatures.reason: Section 17043(a) states the rate and the threshold, and its subdivision (c) states that filing-status recomputation, joint-return treatment and the allowance of credits do not apply to it. The pack carries it as a threshold set that does not vary by filing status and names it in no relief mechanism's applied-legs list.

unsupportedFeatures.label: Rate schedule for the declared tax year
unsupportedFeatures.reason: Section 17041(h) requires the Franchise Tax Board to recompute the brackets for each taxable year, so the dollar amounts printed in the statute are a pre-indexing base rather than the declared year's schedule. The recomputed schedule for the declared year is not published rather than merely unreached: the declared year's own estimated-tax instructions tell the filer to compute tax using the PRIOR year's tax table, which is that authority stating the declared year's table does not yet exist. Every filing status therefore ships an absent figure and the ordinary leg refuses. No bracket is indexed, interpolated, or relabelled from another tax year.
unsupportedFeatures.successorFeature: A pack revision carrying the Franchise Tax Board's recomputed rate schedule for the declared year, transcribed from that publication once it is issued.

unsupportedFeatures.label: Standard deduction for the declared tax year
unsupportedFeatures.reason: Section 17073.5(a) states a pre-indexing base amount and subdivision (d) requires the Franchise Tax Board to recompute the deduction for each taxable year, so the statutory amount is not the declared year's amount. The recomputed amount for the declared year is not published: the declared year's estimated-tax instructions send the filer to the prior year's figures, and the amount that worksheet lists for each filing status is identical to the amount the PRIOR year's Form 540 standard deduction chart lists for the same status, so it states the prior year's amount rather than the declared year's. No amount is carried, none is derived from the federal deduction, none is relabelled from another tax year, and every filing status ships an absent figure.
unsupportedFeatures.successorFeature: A pack revision carrying the standard deduction for the declared year from its own authority once that authority is published.

unsupportedFeatures.label: Personal exemption credit amounts
unsupportedFeatures.reason: Section 17039 establishes that the personal exemption credit is subtracted from the tax imposed under section 17041 and states no amount. Section 17054(a) and (b) state pre-indexing base credits and subdivision (i) requires the Franchise Tax Board to compute the credits for each taxable year, so the statutory amounts are not the declared year's amounts. The computed amounts for the declared year are not published: the declared year's estimated-tax instructions direct the filer to take the exemption credit amount from the PRIOR year's Form 540 instructions. The relief mechanism therefore carries an absent figure per filing status and the credit stage refuses while the legs it would have reduced still resolve.
unsupportedFeatures.successorFeature: A pack revision carrying the exemption credit amounts for the declared year from their own authority once that authority is published.

unsupportedFeatures.label: Itemised deduction
unsupportedFeatures.reason: This pack applies its own standard deduction only. A California itemised deduction and its limitations are not carried, so a household that itemises federally is not told its state deduction is the same figure.
unsupportedFeatures.successorFeature: A deduction feature carrying the state itemised deduction and its limitations.

unsupportedFeatures.label: State alternative minimum tax
unsupportedFeatures.reason: The tentative minimum tax that section 17039(c) refers to is a separate parallel computation and is not carried by this pack.
unsupportedFeatures.successorFeature: A parallel-tax feature carrying the state exemption, phase-out and rate.

unsupportedFeatures.label: Every credit other than the personal exemption credit
unsupportedFeatures.reason: Section 17039(a) lists twelve ordered classes of credit. This pack carries one relief mechanism and no other credit of any kind, including renter, dependent-parent, senior head-of-household and other-state credits.
unsupportedFeatures.successorFeature: A credit feature carrying each credit's amount, ordering class and refundability.

unsupportedFeatures.label: Part-year and non-resident apportionment
unsupportedFeatures.reason: Section 17041(b), (d) and (i) define a separate computation for a non-resident or part-year resident. This pack models single full-year residency only, and any other declared pattern refuses under its own code rather than being approximated.
unsupportedFeatures.successorFeature: An apportionment feature carrying the source rules and the residency-period split.

unsupportedFeatures.label: County and municipal taxes
unsupportedFeatures.reason: No local levy of any kind is carried by this pack, so a household is not told its total local burden is zero.
unsupportedFeatures.successorFeature: A local rule pack resolved by locality, with its own settlement.
